newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends sharply lower after NY tumbles.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends sharply lower after NY tumbles.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa futures closed sharply lower but off daily lows on Monday after a hectic afternoon session when New York gapped down on the open and immediately hit a flurry of sell-stops.
May cocoa ended down 50 stg at 994 stg per tonne and July lost 51 to 1,008. Total volume was heavy at 18,605 contracts.

CSCE cocoa gapped down $25 at the start and then triggered sell-stops near $1,350 and $1,400 as funds liquidated or rolled out of May positions into July before first notice day on April 17 in New York. As of April 3, speculator open interest tallied more than 30,000 lots in New York.
New York's drop pulled LIFFE cocoa sharply lower, with May slipping in early afternoon more than 5.0 percent to the lowest level since March 10, filling two gaps on daily charts.
July also slid but stayed three stg away from completely filling a chart gap between 982 and 998. July's session low on Monday was 985.

Traders said light sell-stops were seen in the morning in July at 1,049, with increasingly heavier sell-stops triggered later in the day at 1,022, 1008 and 998. July support now rests between 985 and 982 and below that at 943.
Cocoa was also pressured by a favourable Ivorian mid-crop outlook as March's rainfall edged up to long-term average levels after a February drought.

Crop analysts in Abidjan said in early March that regular showers up to April would determine how close this year's midcrop would be to the bumper 200,000 tonnes in the record 1.2 million tonnes 1995/96 (Oct-Sept) harvest season.
Though Germany's 11.71-percent fall in first-quarter grinds to 69,520.3 tonnes from year-ago levels was expected, some traders said the figures were still negative for cocoa.

After Monday's volatile session, traders were uncertain where cocoa would head next. They said they would wait to see where New York closed on Monday before making any predictions on cocoa's next move.
